query: For automotive exhaust catalysts, what single intervention could improve catalytic activity and durability while reducing platinum-group-metal consumption? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Coating ceria-based automotive exhaust catalysts with a surface‐confined, atomic high-entropy oxide (HEO) layer composed of first-row transition metals (e.g., Cu, Co, Fe, Ni, Mn) enhances oxygen vacancy formation, which in turn improves catalytic activity and durability while permitting lower platinum-group-metal (PGM) loadings.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional ceria-based catalyst supports used in automotive exhaust catalysts, typically loaded with PGM nanoparticles.
generation.intervention: Deposit an atomic-scale layer of high-entropy oxides (HEOs) composed of multiple first-row transition metal oxides onto the surface of the ceria-based support.
generation.conditions: Catalytic testing under simulated automotive exhaust conditions (high-temperature redox environments) with periodic thermal and chemical cycling.
generation.structural_mediator: The interface between the surface-confined HEO layer and the ceria substrate, where increased covalency and enhanced oxygen vacancy formation occur.
generation.mechanism: The mixed transition metal oxide layer increases the covalent character of the metal–oxygen bonds at the interface, promoting the formation and stabilization of surface oxygen vacancies. This oxygen defect engineering facilitates efficient oxygen activation and replenishment during exhaust oxidation reactions, thereby increasing catalytic activity and durability. The improved reactivity reduces the required loading of costly PGM by enabling more effective catalytic cycles.
generation.predicted_outcome: HEO-coated catalysts will show lower light-off temperatures, improved long-term stability under thermal cycling, and similar or enhanced conversion efficiencies with a reduced PGM loading relative to conventional catalysts.
generation.baseline: Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts featuring ceria supports with standard PGM loadings but without a surface-confined HEO layer.
generation.boundary: This improvement is expected under conditions where the ceria-based supports are amenable to forming and stabilizing oxygen vacancies at the HEO-ceria interface, and may be limited if the interface formation is compromised by severe size mismatch or if the operating temperatures fall outside the reactive regime for vacancy activation.
generation.uncertainty: The long-term chemical compatibility and mechanical integrity of the HEO layer under repeated thermal and chemical cycling in real-world exhaust conditions remain to be fully demonstrated.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of automotive exhaust catalysts: one set with a conventional PGM loading on ceria-based supports (control) and another set with an identical PGM loading reduced by 30-50% but modified with a surface-confined HEO layer. Subject both sets to standardized automotive exhaust simulation tests that include thermal cycling, high-temperature redox conditions, and exposure to typical exhaust gas compositions.
measurements: Light-off temperature (temperature for 50% conversion of exhaust pollutants)
Physical and chemical stability of the HEO layer (via microscopy and spectroscopy)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEO-coated catalysts with reduced PGM loading do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in catalytic activity (i.e., lower light-off temperatures and/or higher TOF) and durability under cycling compared to the control catalysts, or if the structural integrity of the HEO layer degrades rapidly under operating conditions, the hypothesis would be falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractIntroducing transition-metal components to ceria (CeO2) is important to tailor the surface redox properties for a broad scope of applications. The emergence of high-entropy oxides (HEOs) has brought transformative opportunities for oxygen defect engineering in ceria yet has been hindered by the difficulty in controllably introducing transition metals to the bulk lattice of ceria. Here, we report the fabrication of ceria-based nanocrystals with surface-confined atomic HEO layers for enhanced catalysis. The increased covalency of the transition-metal–oxygen bonds at the HEO–CeO2 interface promotes the formation of surface oxygen vacancies, enabling efficient oxygen activation and replenishment for enhanced CO oxidation capabilities. Understanding the structural heterogeneity involving bulk and surface oxygen defects in nanostructured HEOs provides useful insights into rational design of atomically precise metal oxides, whose increased compositional and structural complexities give rise to expanded functionalities. Different from high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with single-site occupancies, independent cation and anion sublattices in HEOs have greater structural tunabilities.− The enhanced configurational entropy gives rise to a higher endurance for lattice distortion. This allows the incorporation and stabilization of a higher concentration of aliovalent metal cations in the oxide lattice, which promotes the activation of lattice oxygen and formation of active species. Additionally, the sluggish kinetics of HEOs introduced improved thermal and chemical stabilities for the metal species under reaction conditions., The entropy-maximization principle has also been extended to the self-regeneration of the HEO-supported metal catalysts.,
Nonetheless, the applicability of this entropy-induced stabilization strategy is limited for ceria-based mixed oxides. The drastic size difference between the first-row transition metal and cerium atoms prompts the formation of oxide–oxide interfaces with inherent structural heterogeneities, which presents a fundamentally distinct scenario relative to the rare-earth-metal-based ceria solid solutions.
